about: Residual differences between two recordings of real Bazel 9.3.2 that normalisation cannot remove. Format and semantics: scripts/oracle/README.md and AllowList in oracle_compare.py. Every entry's condition and max_items are checked on every compare run. max_items is required: per project, how many items the entry excused when the oracle was compared with itself (oracle-9.3.2, -rerun, -check; all three pairs agree); a project that is not named has the cap 0.

entries.condition: The item is a runfiles manifest action (primary output *.runfiles_manifest or *.runfiles/MANIFEST) and actionKey is the only field that differs.
entries.reason: SourceManifestAction's action key fingerprints the manifest content, which names absolute execroot paths. Every recording has its own workspace copy and output base, so the hash differs; the normalised manifest bytes (outputs surface), argv, inputs and outputs still match.

entries.condition: The item is the buildMetrics event and the only differing fields are the per-SkyFunction evaluated/built/changed/cleaned/dirtied counts (and their list order), the post-invocation Skyframe node count, or the action cache's sizeInBytes; or memoryMetrics.garbageMetrics is set on one side only (memoryMetrics itself must be present on both).
entries.reason: Skyframe evaluates in parallel, so how many nodes of each SkyFunction are evaluated or dirtied in one invocation varies between identical runs (re2: a few per cent). The serialized action cache size also varies by a few hundred bytes on re2 (161890 vs 161688) with identical actions and outputs. Action, artifact, target, package and per-mnemonic action counts in the same event are still compared.
entries.jvm_reason: Root's ruling 2026-11-26 (same class as D15): garbageMetrics lists the JVM's garbage-collector memory pools (G1 Eden Space, Metaspace, ...). Blaze has no JVM and prints memoryMetrics without it. A declared deviation of Blaze, not a variation of the oracle: the item counts as allowed, never as matching. Every other memoryMetrics field is still compared by presence.
entries.daemon_mode_reason: Referee batch 3: in oracle-9.3.2, -rerun and -check (brotli, re2) only the evaluatedValues counts, the order of dirtiedValues and (re2) the action cache sizeInBytes vary; builtValues, changedValues and cleanedValues are equal per SkyFunction and in order, and postInvocationSkyframeNodeCount is equal (brotli 7305, re2 23543). Those four fields excuse only a one-process Blaze, which runs the build on a cold server while the oracle's runs on the warm server mod graph started; they are inactive for a candidate recorded in daemon mode.
